artifacts.summary: Isolates and reproduces the prune_next_body() flag-misparse defect (whitespace-stripping fuses a trailing CLI flag onto the last task id, defeating the active-id lookup), confirms an identical sibling defect in count_pruned_next_ids(), confirms layout-independence, confirms zero existing test coverage, and recommends a scoped fix plus required test cases for the plan phase.

memory_candidates.content: Anti-pattern found in roadmap-integration.sh's prune_next_body()/count_pruned_next_ids(): blanket-stripping all whitespace (gsub(/[ \t]/, "", s) or bash ${s//[[:space:]]/}) before splitting an identifier list on commas is unsafe whenever the same line can carry a free-form trailing segment (a CLI flag, a comment) separated from the list by whitespace rather than a comma. The strip silently fuses the last identifier with the following token, defeating any downstream exact-match lookup against that identifier -- with no error. Safer pattern: split off the free-form trailing segment FIRST (on the first run of whitespace, or a known delimiter), then whitespace-strip and comma-split only the identifier-list portion, and re-splice the preserved trailing segment back into any reconstructed output.
